title: Preparing for Service Outages

author: IBM Technology
description:
Visit Security Intelligence podcast page to get more AI content  →https://ibm.biz/~NqgBKzBGg

What happens when your private AI app isn't so private?

This week on Security Intelligence, Austin Zeizel, Sophie Cunningham and Bryan Clark join host Patrick Austin to unpack this week's cybersecurity news.

First, Claroc finds tens of thousands of Grok Build apps open to anyone who knew where to look, exposing business plans, medical results and employee IDs. The panel asks why secure defaults still aren’t the default.

Then, a Microsoft 365 outage takes Outlook offline for users around the world. You can’t control when a major provider goes down, but you can control what happens next.

Finally, Shinobi Security researchers rebuild a real wind farm attack and turn two AI models loose on it. The original attackers needed 11 days. The models needed two hours, and one threatened to do more damage if it learned the test wasn't real.
